sentences.text: Ammonitritor is an extinct early ichthyosauriform that belongs to the family Omphalosauridae and lived during the Early Triassic Olenekian stage in the Vikinghøgda Formation of Norway.
The only specimen known includes a nearly complete skull together with a partial vertebral column.
It is the first omphalosaurid for which a three-dimensional skull has been recovered, whereas other members are known only from flattened skulls.
The fossil was uncovered by Felix Saludes during a 2010 expedition led by Luc Ebbo on the northwest slope of Vikinghøgda mountain in Svalbard, Norway.
The material is catalogued as PGE LE 2024.0.264 and is stored in Luc Ebbo's Paléogalerie in Salignac, France.
Although the skull is partially disarticulated and missing the braincase and palate, the preserved elements retain their original three-dimensional shape.
Ammonitritor, like other omphalosaurids, had extensive maxillary and dentary tooth batteries that were suited for grinding hard-shelled cephalopods such as ammonoids.
Phylogenetic analysis places Ammonitritor within Omphalosauridae, branching after Cartorhynchus and before Sclerocormus and Omphalosaurus.
